data_card.measured: USGS indirect peak-discharge measurements on Hudson, Tiber and New Cut Branches, and high-water marks, for the floods of 30 July 2016 and 27 May 2018.
data_card.method: Post-flood USGS surveys: indirect (slope-area or similar) discharge measurements and flagged high-water marks; UAS survey of the district in 2018.
data_card.uncertainty: Indirect discharge measurements are typically uncertain by tens of percent; to be taken from the USGS computations.
known_issues: Debris, vehicles and building damage changed the flow paths during the event.
data_card.exercises: Steep urban flash flooding: supercritical street flow, flow around buildings and rapid rise.
data_card.cannot_tell: With rainfall-runoff upstream as an input, a miss may be in the hydrology rather than the hydraulics; debris is outside what any shallow-water model represents.

events.notes: The second flood, scored with the set-up calibrated on the first.

validation_design.holdout_policy: A set-up calibrated on 2016 is scored on 2018 unchanged, apart from the event's own inflow.

title: Ellicott City, Maryland, 30 July 2016 flash flood
description: Urban flash flood down steep streets, against USGS indirect peak-discharge measurements and high-water marks on the three streams through the historic district.

citations.title: Storms and floods of July 30, 2016, and May 27, 2018, in Ellicott City, Howard County, Maryland

provenance.adaptation_notes: Draft: high-water marks, indirect discharge sections, terrain and rainfall to be assembled; the 2018 flood gives a second event.
